items.title: Same-sex partner medical rights plea: Delhi HC asks how media got Centre's affidavit beforehand
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday asked how the Central government's written response to a plea seeking recognition of same-sex partners as each other's medical representatives was reported by the media before it was placed before the Court. Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said that the Court was surprised when it read the Centre's reply in the media. "How is the counter known to the press before I came to know? I am very surprised. I read it and I was just thinking, ye case toh mere pass hai. Press ke pass kaise pehle aata hai? (How does it come to the press first?) I am also intrigued. How is it that you have given a copy to them and to the ress? Somebody has given it to the press." Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma responded that the government had not shared the counter affidavit with the media. "We have not given it to the press. The government does not give it to the press. That is the reason, the matter may have some other connotation. Today I am not saying anything. SG will," he said. items.title: Karnataka sacks Congress MLA’s niece for drawing Rs 75,000 salary without doing work
items.summary: Karnataka authorities relieved Dr Ankita R Yaragal, niece of Bagalkot Congress MLA Umesh Meti, from her post as a medical officer at a Namma Clinic, on Thursday, September 17, after allegations that she was drawing a monthly salary of Rs 75,000 while pursuing an MD course at a private medical college. Dr Ankita was appointed as a contractual medical officer at the Namma Clinic in Wambe Colony in Bagalkot town in April 2025. She is the daughter of Bagalkot District Health Officer (DHO) Dr Rajkumar Yaragal. The matter came to light after Bagalkot Taluk Health Officer (THO) Dr Saraswati Magi visited the clinic a few days ago and found Dr Ankita absent. When contacted over the phone, she reportedly said that she was out of station. Patients allegedly told the THO that the doctor had not been attending the clinic for around three months, although her attendance was intact. Residents had reportedly complained that doctors were not regularly attending the Namma Clinic and that nurses were managing patients and dispensing medicines. Dr Ankita had joined an MD programme in Pathology at a private medical college in March 2026 while continuing to serve as a medical officer at the Namma Clinic

On February 28, 2026, the first sighting of a Demoiselle Crane was reported from Chennai Metropolitan Area. The only other records of Demoiselle Crane sighting from Tamil Nadu comes from Vijayanarayanam Tank in Tirunelveli. Naman Bora and Amoggh Chatty found the vagrant bird feeding in the reeds at Nemmeli salt pans near Chennai; the former would return to the spot the next three days and find the bird tenaciously clinging to this feeding spot
